item.title: Local reaction as increase of pint cost comes into effect
item.description: A pub owner in Co Cavan says the increase in the price of a pint puts pressure on rural pubs. Dean McMullen is co-owner of the Burnt Pig in Cootehill, the pub opened it's doors just before Christmas of 2025. In January Diageo announced a further price increase, which is the fifth increase seen in three years. item.title: Monaghan Fire Chief issues safety appeal over flood water
item.description: With more rainfall expected across the region over the next 48 hours, Monaghan's Chief Fire Officer has outlined the importance of adhering to safety guidelines. According to Dermot Brannigan, relatively intense rainfall over a short time period last week had a serious impact on rivers across Co Monaghan which had already reached their max. item.title: Mixed fortunes for Basketball teams in the region
item.description: Utility Trust St Pauls Killarney maintained their top of the table position with a 63 -41 win over Mc Evoy Cavan Eagles in the Womens Super League over the weekend. That result ended the Breffni sides winning run and sees them hold 6th place in the league table. item.title: Local calls for increased payments to farmers after TB
item.description: A local TD has called for the Department of Agriculture to examine the compensation paid to farmers who have to cull animals after an outbreak of a disease. Fine Gael TD, David Maxwell, raised the issue with the Minister for Agriculture in the Dáil last week (Thursday, January 29th). Deputy Maxwell highlighted the financial and mental toll that an outbreak of disease, such as TB or birdflu, can have for farmers. item.title: Cavan Senator: 'Councils are chronically underfunded'
item.description: A Co. Cavan Senator believes that county councils do not receive enough funding for roads. Aontú Senator Sarah O'Reilly raised the issue in the Seanad last week (Thursday, January 29th). According to Senator O'Reilly, in 2021 Cavan County Council received €508,000 for maintenance. item.title: Calls for Govt to take 'stern approach' to forestry
item.description: There have been calls for the Electricity Supply Amendment Bill to be completed without any further delay. Local TD, Brendan Smith stressed that enhanced electricity resilience is essential to protect customers, particularly in rural and vulnerable areas Deputy Smith said that placing forestry corridors on a statutory footing is critical, noting that people cannot be left without electricity in light of the increasingly severe and frequent weather events experienced in recent years. item.title: Julie Richards-Whitaker
item.description: Julie Richards-Whitaker Coas, Tullynahinnera, Castleblayney, Monaghan. Julie Richards-Whitaker passed away on Monday, February 2nd, 2026. Peacefully, in the care of the nurses and staff at Our Lady Of Lourdes Hospital Drogheda. Predeceased by her mother Philomena Karachi (Née Hopkins) and her son Graham. Deeply regretted and lovingly remembered by her family, her devoted husband Victor Whitaker, her daughter Lucy Townson, her grandson Sonny, her cousins, extended family, neighbours and friends.

item.title: Local homeless charity issue appeal for volunteers
item.description: A local homeless charity has issued a call out for volunteers to to help continue supporting those most in need. Help Our Homeless who are based in Kingscourt is desperately seeking volunteers to help people who are living on the streets of Dublin. They are currently looking for drivers to help with collections and outreach in Dublin along with volunteers in both Cavan and Monaghan.
